the forced expression of choline acetyltrans­ferase in FB5 cells results in the enhancement of the differentiated phenotype, as revealed by increased expression of acetylcholines­terase, voltage‐gated sodium channels, and high‐affinity uptake of choline, and in the acquisition of the ability to respond to the neurotransmitter acetylcholine.
the expression of choline acetyl transferase, in a cell type that does not normally express it, induces the expression of a more advanced neuronal phenotype.
the expression of a neuronal marker, such as choline acetyl transferase, can modify the expression of other neuronal markers and, therefore, can modulate the differentiation process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of the choline acetylation pathway leads to an increase of the differentiated phenotype of the neuroblastoma cell line.
the choline acetylation pathway is involved in the regulation of the expression of neuronal differentiation traits.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the modulation of acetylcholineserterase activity and of voltage‐gged Na+ channels in the FB5 subline of N18TG neuroblastoma cells transfected with cDNAs for choline acetytransferase may be an important factor in the acquisition of a more differentiated neuronal phenotype.
acetylcholine may play a role as a morphogenic factor in neuronal development.
acetylcholine, through its enzymatic degradation and through the activation of its specific receptors, may play a significant role in the modulation and regulation of neuronal differentiation.
